settings.description: Show a plain-language answer first; hide developer detail behind “More technical detail”.
Label for the expandable technical section under assistant replies.
File head lines used when entry-point grep has no keyword match.

usage.whenEnable: Entry files lack keyword overlap — need more head lines from main.py, api.py, etc.
usage.whenDisable: Grep snippets are too large for tight token budgets.
pros: Helps overview when keywords miss file headers

settings.description: Max entry-point grep snippets on architecture and overview questions.

usage.whenEnable: Architecture or “how does this repo work?” prompts need more entry-point file snippets.
usage.whenDisable: Overview answers already cite main.py, api.py, and the extension — reduce grep competition.
pros: Boosts entry-point anchors for high-level architecture questions
cons: More grep slots on a query type sensitive to noise
usage.recommendation: Leave default unless entry paths are missing from overview answers.

settings.description: Grep the local workspace before chat and send hits to the server (demo / indexing handoff).

usage.whenEnable: Demo visibility, indexing handoff, or symbol-heavy prompts where local workspace search helps before server retrieval.
usage.whenDisable: Noisy local paths polluting architecture or overview answers; reduce client-side work on large monorepos.
pros: Surfaces open-file and keyword hits before the stream starts
Useful while the index is still building (with indexingOnly)
cons: Can pull in docs, session packs, or non-code files into context
Server still budgets and may down-rank meta paths on overview questions
usage.recommendation: Keep enabled for development; tighten grep limits if overview answers feel noisy.

settings.description: When true, client grep runs only while the workspace index is building.

usage.whenEnable: Limit grep noise after the index is ready — search locally only while indexing is in progress.
usage.whenDisable: You rely on client grep for every chat turn (demos, offline symbol lookup).
pros: Faster sends when the index is ready
cons: No client-side path hints after indexing completes
usage.recommendation: Consider enabling on laptops with limited RAM after the index is ready.

settings.description: Keep the Reasoning panel expanded after chat when local grep found files (demo visibility).

Max workspace files scanned per client grep pass.

usage.whenEnable: Large workspaces where keyword search needs a wider scan (slower).
usage.whenDisable: Performance issues or excessive grep time before send.
usage.recommendation: Lower on laptops if compose feels sluggish.

settings.description: Max grep snippets sent with each chat request.

usage.whenEnable: Raise briefly for dense symbol-navigation demos.
usage.whenDisable: Lower (e.g. 4–6) when sources feel noisy or the token budget is tight.

cons: More tokens competing with packs and server retrieval on overview prompts
usage.recommendation: Default 8 is balanced; lower if sources look cluttered.

retrievalGuide.title: Retrieval & context assembly (extension)
retrievalGuide.summary: These VS Code settings control what the extension adds before the API assembles context. They complement — but do not replace — server-side structural flags below. High-level architecture answers are mostly shaped on the server; local grep can still add noise if left wide open after indexing finishes.
tips: For “how does this repo work?” questions, keep client grep reasonable and let indexing finish first.
For “how is this route registered?” questions, server structural flags matter more than extension grep.
If answers cite the wrong files, lower clientGrepMaxSnippets or enable clientGrepIndexingOnly.
